thread:
susan (ACME): Help — user we deprovisioned last week came back after our Okta org merge. They were removed via SCIM but now there's a new account with same email in different case and it's in a private workspace.

emily (CSE): can you paste the Okta event ids and our SCIM request/response log? We need the sequence to repro.

susan (ACME): Okta timeline snippets: `2024-06-03T09:12:04Z DELETE /Users/00uX1111 204` (deprovisioner). Then `2024-06-03T09:14:33Z POST /Users 201` (group.push/import). POST payload has `emails:[{value:"Jane.Doe+sales@Example.COM", primary:true}]` and no `externalId`.

okta-bot: event -> type: group.push, action: createUser, source: org-synchronization

harry (SRE): on our side we logged the outgoing delete as 204. After the POST we recorded `PATCH /Users/00uY2222 200` setting `active=true` and then several Group membership PATCHes. So a new user row was created then activated and granted the team.

jorge (Eng): theory: our resolver keyed deletes by internal user id and externalId. When the POST had no externalId and email had a plus-tag and case changes, our matching path didn't normalize email consistently so it created a new user. The subsequent PATCH completed provisioning.

susan (ACME): correct, two user rows in console: 00uX1111 (deleted) and 00uY2222 (active). same display name, email differs only by case and `+sales` tag.

emily (CSE): risk: reappearance after deprovision is a security/visitor risk. Need mitigation ASAP and a plan to avoid recurrence.

harry (SRE): immediate actions: 1) pause Okta group-push for the affected tenant (ACME) — can you do that, susan? 2) run a dry-run dedupe to find collisions by canonical email (lowercase, strip `+` tags for known providers). I'll produce CSV of candidates: `deleted_id,new_id,canonical_email,okta_event_ids`.

susan (ACME): pausing group-push now.

jorge (Eng): medium-term fixes: - make email canonicalization consistent across create/update/delete paths (`toLowerCase()` + provider alias rules), - prefer `externalId` when present, - treat POSTs from group-push as conditional upserts: if no externalId and email canonical matches deleted tombstone, map to deleted user instead of creating, - add short TTL tombstone on delete for email aliases (30 days).

harry (SRE): dry-run finished: found 5 suspects for ACME, two with plus-tags and three with casing differences. Uploaded CSV to the shared drive and linked it in thread. Final cleanup scheduled 2024-06-03T16:00Z after review.

emily (CSE): assigning owners: @jorge to implement normalization + tombstone logic behind feature flag; @harry to run cleanup and coordinate the final revoke; @susan to keep group-push paused until we say go. Goal: PR by EOD, cleanup after verification.

jorge (Eng): dev notes: canonical function should be pluggable per-idp rules. Implement `canonicalEmail(email, provider)` where provider rules strip `+` tags for gmail-like domains, remove dots for gmail if configured, and always lowercase. On delete store `email_aliases: [canonical_email, known_variants]` with `deleted_user_id` and TTL. POST handling: if `externalId` present match by externalId; else compute canonical and check existing active or tombstoned entries. If tombstoned, mark create as reattach rather than fresh create.

harry (SRE): operational checklist for cleanup: - run dedupe dry-run, review with CSE, generate mapping CSV, run final job which will merge or delete the phantom accounts, and log actions. One-liner used for canonicalization included in CSV upload.

susan (ACME): thanks — we've kept group-push paused and reviewing the CSV. We'll confirm before final job.

emily (CSE): follow-ups: add telemetry counters `scim.create_from_group_push`, `scim.create_after_delete`, and an alert if `create_after_delete` > threshold. Also include an audit of recent deletions to ensure no mass re-creates.

jorge (Eng): I'll open PR with tests for: plus-tag handling, casing-only matches, and tombstone mapping. Feature flag by default off for rollout.

emily (CSE): good, keep this channel updated when PR lands and after the 16:00 cleanup. Thanks everyone.
